$comment: Which migrations belong to Veylith's own company layer rather than to the
WHY A MANIFEST RATHER THAN A MARKER IN THE SQL
A `-- migrate:layer company` line inside the file would be the obvious
design and it cannot be used: the runner refuses a migration whose
checksum has changed since it was applied, and adding a line changes the
checksum. That refusal is correct and worth more than the tidiness, so the
classification lives beside the files instead of inside them.
The usual cost of a manifest is that it drifts from what it describes.
migration whose SQL touches the `veylith` schema must be listed here, and
anything listed here must actually touch it. Neither direction can rot
